history.scope: controlled contrastive quality, bounded operational probes, and deterministic provenance workflow

history.status: frozen before scoring the new external selected-rule set or running the integrated production-path experiment

amendments.stage: after preliminary controlled scoring and before the final clean-commit run
changes: Use paired contrastive cases rather than claiming every pair is a minimal textual edit.
Report direct warmed judge-call latency and hook-process/IPC probes as separate boundaries.
Treat the originally planned event-to-outcome, resource, and matched Codex-turn measurements as not evaluated by protocol 1.1.0; they support no claim from that study.
amendments.reason: The original synthetic harness identifies process and IPC boundaries but cannot infer user-visible Codex latency or production resource behavior.

amendments.stage: after preliminary local scoring and before the final controlled clean-commit run
changes: Add one separately prompted open-model judge baseline (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507) using deterministic decoding and the same strict output parser.
amendments.reason: User-provided ALL-partition GPU capacity made a reproducible larger-model calibration baseline feasible.

amendments.stage: before scoring the external selected-rule set and before running the integrated experiment
changes: Add an eight-rule selected-instruction challenge set whose rule intent comes from a pinned CC-BY-4.0 public instruction corpus and whose balanced inputs and labels are synthetic by construction.
Add paired PAW-minus-baseline contrasts over the already frozen controlled outputs; report this as a transparent post-hoc inferential analysis anchored to protocol 1.1.0.
Add an isolated full production-path experiment using the installed Codex wrapper, Unix socket, daemon, deployed rule revision, frozen PAW artifact, SQLite store, and verdict query API.
Measure query-visible findings, not rendered menu-bar latency or Codex turn latency.
unchanged: protocol-1.1.0 controlled rule sources, inputs, labels, predictions, and manifests
amendments.reason: The paper needs evidence beyond the four controlled rules and direct integrated-runtime measurements while preserving the original measurement boundaries.

research_questions.rq1: How reliably do local compiled rules classify controlled, paired-contrast coding-agent events?
research_questions.rq2: What direct-judge latency and ingress reliability behavior can be established at explicitly instrumented local boundaries?
research_questions.rq3: Does RAP preserve the exact managed-rule input and revision provenance needed for a deterministic inspect-and-refine workflow?
research_questions.rq4: How well do the systems classify synthetic contrastive events for eight purposively selected, externally sourced instruction atoms?
research_questions.rq5: Across the installed hook-to-store path, what query-visible finding latency, loss, duplication, burst-drain behavior, resource use, and isolated recovery behavior are observed?

external_selected_rules.name: rap-external-selected-rules-v1
external_selected_rules.selection: purposive eligibility screen for one-event, one-field observability plus behavior diversity; one extracted instruction atom per repository
external_selected_rules.selection_limit: not a random, representative, or prevalence sample; no claim about the fraction of public instructions expressible by RAP or performance outside these selected rules
external_selected_rules.instruction_provenance: external public corpus, with an explicitly documented one-field sub-rule when the source record contains multiple obligations
external_selected_rules.input_provenance: synthetic contrastive pairs with labels fixed by construction
external_selected_rules.case_authorship: rule specifications and synthetic cases were co-designed; only exact reuse of specification examples is forbidden

primary_metrics.controlled: mean across rules of positive-class F1
primary_metrics.external_selected_rules: mean across the eight selected rules of positive-class F1

secondary_metrics: external fixed-rule, within-rule pair bootstrap 95% confidence intervals
paired exact correctness tests with Holm adjustment where multiple baseline contrasts are reported

bootstrap.external_primary_resampling: keep all eight purposively selected rules fixed and, within each rule, sample ten complete contrastive pairs with replacement
bootstrap.external_exploratory_sensitivity: hierarchical rule-then-pair resampling, reported only as a sensitivity analysis and not as population-level uncertainty

failure_injections: terminate the isolated PAW worker after warm measurements and require the next event to produce a finding
gracefully stop and restart the isolated daemon and require the next event to produce a finding
integrated_experiment.start_boundary: parent immediately before launching the installed project hook wrapper
integrated_experiment.end_boundary: first successful daemon verdict query returning the exact evaluated input
excluded: Codex scheduling of its asynchronous hook
rendering or human perception of the macOS menu-bar UI
remote compilation because the deployed PAW artifact is already frozen

exclusions: inputs exceeding the rule byte limit
exact copies of examples embedded in the frozen specification
any native event not manually approved for release

claim_gates.external_selected_rules_accurate: macro positive-class F1 >= 0.80 on the complete frozen eight-rule selected-instruction challenge set
claim_gates.integrated_sequential_reliable: zero missing findings and zero duplicate findings
claim_gates.integrated_burst_reliable: zero missing findings at burst size 24
claim_gates.integrated_recovery: both isolated worker replacement and daemon restart yield a query-visible finding within 20 seconds

failure_policy.external_selected_rules: retain every frozen case and every per-case invalid output or runtime error after system preparation succeeds; a compiler or model preparation failure marks that complete system run unavailable and supports no partial score; do not drop a hard rule or selectively rerun cases
failure_policy.integrated: the canonical run either completes every declared invariant and writes one result or is reported as a failed study run with no performance claim; do not selectively rerun a failed canonical execution without a dated protocol amendment
failure_policy.deviations: record any protocol change with stage, reason, and unchanged elements before using the affected result
